title: Managed AI building blocks and platform choices
summary: Foundation-model access, AI Functions, serving endpoints, the AI Gateway, Agent Bricks and custom agents: placed by who writes the logic, chosen with five criteria, and recorded with dated status, cost and evaluation assumptions.
outcomes: Distinguish pay-per-token, provisioned-throughput and external-model access, AI Functions, Agent Bricks agents and custom agents by who writes the logic and who hosts it.
State which AI Gateway controls apply to which endpoint types, citing a named and dated artifact.
Choose a pattern with a decision table on customization, data access, operations, evaluation and risk, including when a fixed retrieval workflow beats autonomous tool selection.
Build responsibility, availability and cost-assumption tables with unknown cells and check-current-pricing rates.
Plan an evaluation that compares candidate patterns on one labelled question set under rules agreed in advance.
startingAssumptions: The GenAI module's separation of retrieval, generation, tools and evaluation is familiar.
Unity Catalog grants and model versions are familiar; nothing here needs a workspace, a paid service or a model call.
editorialRationale: Platform choices go wrong when a newer managed pattern is treated as the default or a status is inferred from an announcement, so the module first places every building block by who writes the logic above the model, then treats model access, AI Functions, serving, the AI Gateway, Agent Bricks agents and custom agents as separate responsibilities before a decision table, responsibility, status and cost tables and a comparative evaluation. Every product fact is tied to a named artifact read in this build with its version and date, and every availability and price stays a verification item.

concepts.definition: One of the platform's ways to put a model to work, distinguished by who writes the logic between a request and the model: an application, a SQL author, the platform or the team's own agent code.
concepts.example: Cinderline's nightly labelling uses an AI Function; its technician assistant uses a Knowledge Assistant.

concepts.definition: A Databricks-hosted foundation-model endpoint charged by the tokens each request processes, with no capacity to size and the endpoint's usage limits applying.
concepts.example: Cinderline's pilot asks a hosted model 300 questions a day and pays for those tokens only.

concepts.definition: Reserved serving capacity for one foundation model, sized in model units with optional burst scaling, charged for the capacity kept provisioned rather than the tokens used.
concepts.example: An endpoint for one hosted model sized at a number of model units for steady production traffic.

aliases: Mosaic AI Model Serving external model
concepts.definition: A serving endpoint whose served entity forwards requests to a named outside provider using a key referenced from a secret scope, adding Databricks permissions and gateway controls in front.
concepts.example: An endpoint forwarding chat requests to an OpenAI model with the key stored in a secret scope.

concepts.definition: The general-purpose AI Function that sends each row's request from a SQL query to a model serving endpoint the caller names.
concepts.example: A query summarizing 200 work-order notes by calling a named endpoint once per note.

concepts.definition: A built-in AI Function that performs one fixed task, such as classifying text into supplied labels, with a model managed by Databricks.
concepts.example: ai_classify labels each note electrical, hydraulic or mechanical.

concepts.definition: A REST endpoint on Databricks-managed serverless compute that serves one or more models or agents as served entities, with traffic routes and CAN_QUERY permission for callers.
concepts.example: The endpoint hosting Cinderline's manuals agent, queried by the tablet app's service principal.

concepts.definition: A serving endpoint that hosts an agent rather than a bare model, created by the agent framework's deploy() or by an Agent Bricks agent.
concepts.example: The endpoint a Knowledge Assistant reports as its endpoint_name.

concepts.definition: Configuration on a serving endpoint for rate limits, guardrails, usage tracking, inference tables and fallback, whose supported features depend on the endpoint type.
concepts.example: A rate limit of 10 calls per minute on the endpoint key plus PII blocking on input and output.

concepts.definition: An AI Gateway filter on requests or responses, such as a safety filter or PII detection set to block or mask, applied where the endpoint type supports it.
concepts.example: A PII guardrail set to BLOCK on input rejects a prompt containing a phone number.

concepts.definition: A Unity Catalog table where an endpoint's AI Gateway logs request and response payloads for monitoring, auditing and later evaluation.
concepts.example: The agent endpoint's payload table sampled monthly into Cinderline's evaluation set.

concepts.definition: Databricks agents built by the platform from configuration such as sources, tools, instructions and examples; in the artifacts read here they include Knowledge Assistants, Supervisor Agents and Custom LLMs. Databricks developer documentation also uses Agent Bricks as the name of its whole agent platform, custom Python agents included; this module's Agent Bricks agents are the configured ones.
concepts.example: Cinderline configures a Knowledge Assistant instead of writing retrieval code.

concepts.definition: An Agent Bricks agent that answers questions from configured knowledge sources (a vector search index, volume files or a file table) guided by instructions and examples, served on its own agent endpoint.
concepts.example: An assistant over 2,400 manuals and a bulletin index answering technicians with citations.

concepts.definition: An Agent Bricks agent that decides per request which configured tools, such as Knowledge Assistants, Genie Agents or Unity Catalog functions, to call before answering.
concepts.example: A supervisor sending torque questions to the manuals assistant and stock questions to a function.

concepts.definition: A design in which a model chooses per request which tools to call, adding a routing decision that can choose wrongly, skip a tool or reach one the caller may not use.
concepts.example: The supervisor answering a stock question from a manual's spares list instead of the stock function.

concepts.definition: Agent logic written as code, wrapped with MLflow's ResponsesAgent and owned and tested by the team that wrote it; Databricks recommends running it in a Databricks App, while deploying it with the agent framework's deploy() to its own agent endpoint, after registering it in Unity Catalog, is the legacy path.
concepts.example: Cinderline's own manuals agent that always searches the newest manual revision first.

concepts.definition: A pipeline that takes the same steps for every question: retrieve permitted passages, answer from them with citations or refuse when none qualifies.
concepts.example: Retrieve plant-scoped manual passages, refuse below a threshold, else answer citing manual and revision.

concepts.definition: A table scoring every candidate pattern in words on customization, data access, operations, evaluation and risk after hard constraints have filtered the candidates.
concepts.example: Cinderline's table comparing ai_query, a Knowledge Assistant, a Supervisor Agent and a custom agent.

concepts.definition: The separation between who runs a component, who decides its data and access, and who is charged for it, recorded per component of a design.
concepts.example: Databricks hosts the endpoint; Cinderline governs the manuals and grants and pays usage.

concepts.definition: A dated label on a named artifact describing a feature's support level, distinct from availability in a given cloud, region or workspace.
concepts.example: The Terraform provider v1.133.0 page labels the Knowledge Assistant resource Public Beta.

concepts.definition: An estimate that multiplies countable synthetic volumes by named drivers, leaves every rate to current pricing and is replaced by measured usage after a pilot.
concepts.example: 300 questions a day times about 3,400 tokens, rate: check current pricing.

concepts.definition: One set of labelled questions with expected facts, sources and refusals, run against every candidate pattern under rules agreed before any result.
concepts.example: Sixty technician questions scored on a Knowledge Assistant and a fixed workflow.

concepts.definition: A Unity Catalog securable that routes inference requests to pay-per-token, provisioned-throughput or external destinations with fallback, rate limits and an inference table under schema-level privileges.
concepts.example: A model service in a maintenance schema routing all traffic to one hosted model.

concepts.definition: A gateway server shipped in the open-source MLflow package and hosted by whoever runs it, distinct from Databricks-managed endpoint configuration.
concepts.example: A team running the MLflow gateway on its own host in front of two providers.

concepts.definition: An Agent Bricks resource holding instructions, guidelines, an endpoint name and labelled Unity Catalog datasets used for training and evaluation, with an optimization lifecycle.
concepts.example: A custom LLM for summarizing work orders trained and evaluated on a labelled notes table.

concepts.definition: The MLflow experiment that deploy() attaches to an agent endpoint so production traces are logged and monitored, found from the environment, an existing monitor or the active experiment.
concepts.example: mlflow.set_experiment('/Shared/cinderline-manuals-agent') run before agents.deploy().
